title: There’s a reason the Bible goes quiet about them.
paragraphs: There’s a reason the Bible goes quiet about them.
Not completely silent—but just enough to make you lean in.

You read past the names quickly at first. A strange pair of words buried in priestly garments, ancient rituals, decisions made in shadows. The Urim and Thummim. Mysterious. Unexplained. Almost… hidden.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
And you don’t have it the way you think you do.
The first time you encounter them is in Book of Exodus:
“And you shall put in the breastpiece of judgment the Urim and the Thummim, and they shall be on Aaron’s heart when he goes in before the Lord…” (Exodus 28:30)
Not in his hand. Not on a shelf.
The high priest would stand before God carrying the burden of the people—and somehow, through these mysterious instruments, God would answer.
And the people depended on it.
Sacred objects used to discern divine will? Almost certainly.
In Book of 1 Samuel and Book of Numbers, leaders like Saul and Joshua sought God’s direction through them. Sometimes there was an answer.
And only one man—one—could approach God in this way.
You think you want that system?
But God never worked that way.
The Urim and Thummim disappear from the narrative. No clear mention after the exile. No explanation.
In Book of Hebrews, it says:
“In the past God spoke to our ancestors through the prophets at many times and in various ways, but in these last days He has spoken to us by His Son…” (Hebrews 1:1–2)
Jesus Christ is the final and full revelation of God.
The Urim and Thummim were never the point.
They were a shadow of something greater.
A temporary system pointing to a permanent Savior.
You don’t need sacred objects to hear from God.
But that doesn’t mean you’re listening.
You justify things you know are wrong.
And still—you say you’re “waiting for direction.”
“Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” (Psalm 119:105)
The issue isn’t that God is silent.
The issue is that His voice confronts you.
The mystery isn’t what the Urim and Thummim were.
The mystery is why you’re still looking for signs when the cross already answered everything.
At the cross, your sin was exposed.
“But God demonstrates His own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” (Romans 5:8)
You can keep searching for signs.
Hoping for clarity while ignoring conviction.
You can respond to what God has already made clear:
And salvation is found in Jesus Christ alone.
There are deeper truths waiting—Scripture that will confront you, correct you, and lead you out of confusion into clarity.
If something in you is stirring right now, don’t ignore it.
And you already know who needs to see this. Send it to them. Because some people are still chasing signs when they’re one step away from surrender.
